label: Service agreement gross margin
definition: Gross margin on recurring service-agreement (maintenance) revenue. n=259 companies with at least $10K in SA revenue.
note: Contractors below 25% are typically underpricing SAs or not capturing maintenance pull-through.

label: Annual service agreement pull-through
definition: Additional repair, replacement, and project revenue from service-agreement customers divided by annual service-agreement revenue. n=386 eligible companies.
basis: 386 companies with eligible annual agreement and follow-on revenue
note: P90 includes relationship-driven project work attributed to service-agreement accounts, not only work discovered during maintenance visits. P75 is the more realistic operating comparison. Company-level records are not published because the underlying roster is re-identifiable; this public file exposes only the aggregate distribution.

label: Annual service agreement revenue per employee
definition: Annual service-agreement revenue divided by employee count. This is a directional Level engagement observation across 217 eligible companies, not a universal staffing target.
basis: 217 companies with eligible annual service-agreement revenue and employee counts
note: Use the distribution as recurring-revenue intensity context. Trade mix, use of subcontractors, and which employees are included can materially change the ratio.
source: The Level Index (directional contractor benchmark observation)

label: Collection rate
definition: Cash collected as a share of billed revenue.
note: The gap between 85% and 96% is real cash: on $5M of billings, ~$550K sitting uncollected.

label: Billing speed (days from work complete to invoice)
definition: Days from job completion to invoice issued. Median is 1 day when progress billing is included (~25% of companies); among post-completion invoicers the adjusted median is 7 days.

label: Billing capture rate (hours invoiced / hours logged on jobs)
definition: Total hours invoiced to customers divided by total hours LOGGED ON JOBS. The denominator is job-assigned hours only, which is why the median is high. This is NOT technician utilization: the industry utilization benchmark (65-80%) divides billable hours by TOTAL PAID hours, including drive time, admin, training, and idle time. Values above 100% occur where overtime hours bill at premium rates. n=963 companies with at least 100 logged hours.
note: State the denominator whenever this is cited. Without it the figure reads implausible, because readers compare it to utilization, which measures something else. First derived 2026-04-07 as 'billable hour ratio' (median 96.7%, n=654) and re-run to 97.1% on the larger n=963 cohort.

label: Quote conversion rate (on decided quotes)
definition: Won divided by (won + lost); excludes still-pending quotes. n=794 companies with at least 20 decided quotes. Distinct from all-quote conversion below.
note: Quotes that sit >7 days convert at roughly half the rate of quotes sent within 24 hours.

label: Average billed labor rate by company
definition: Company-level average billed labor rate across 1,770 contractors. The underlying rate-card field is used inconsistently, with some companies entering customer billing rates and others entering loaded cost or base wage, so the distribution is strongest as a market-positioning comparison.
basis: 1,770 companies with a calculated average billed labor rate
note: These are labor-component rates per technician hour, not the total customer invoice after trip charges, materials, equipment, and overhead markup.

label: Quote conversion rate (all quotes issued)
definition: Won divided by all quotes issued, including quotes that never reach a decision.
note: Roughly 62% of total quoting effort produces zero revenue.

label: Days to convert (winning quotes)
definition: Days from quote sent to accepted, for quotes that convert.
note: Winning quotes close fast; speed-to-decision is the strongest leading indicator.

label: Days to loss (lost quotes)
definition: Days from quote sent to marked lost, for quotes that do not convert.
note: Half of lost quotes linger past 30 days before anyone marks them dead.

label: Revenue from largest single customer
definition: Share of total revenue from the top 1 customer. n=959 companies with at least $100K in annual revenue.

label: Job-level gross margin
definition: Gross margin per completed job (revenue minus actual cost), across all job types. Measured per JOB across 1,747,089 completed jobs from 1,791 companies (Athena verification 2026-07-25). The prior n=430 was another metric's company count.

label: Labor hours: actual as % of budgeted
observation_unit: jobs with budgeted and actual hours
definition: Actual labor hours ÷ budgeted labor hours per job. 100% = on budget; >100% = over. Measured across 315,393 jobs from 1,391 companies (Athena verification 2026-07-25).
basis: jobs with both budgeted and actual hours
note: Median job lands on budget (99.4%) but the mean is 119%, dragged up by the ~18% of jobs that exceed 150% of budget. Labor-hour overruns are the single largest margin killer; 40% of jobs exceed their hour budget.

label: Labor share of quoted revenue
definition: Labor as a share of quoted revenue (vs materials, equipment, subs). Median contractor is ~29% labor / ~33% materials, but variance is extreme. NOTE: sample size unverified. The prior n=430 was copied from another metric; this is measured on quoted revenue (quote-line data), not job_stats, so a job-level reproduction does not apply. Do not publish a sample size until re-derived.
note: Labor-heavy contractors run higher margins but hit capacity limits; materials-heavy run lower margins but scale better.

label: Job closeout lag (days)
definition: Days from work complete to job financially closed out. Cash sits on the table while closeout lags.

label: Revenue concentration in top 3 months
definition: Share of annual revenue earned in the three strongest months.
note: The median contractor earns ~47% of annual revenue in just 3 months; Q4 (Dec/Oct) dominates peaks.

label: Quote-line gross margin by cost type
definition: Gross margin on quoted work, split by cost type (labor, materials, equipment, subcontractor), measured across 2.2M+ quote line items. Labor is the highest-margin cost type; subcontractor pass-through is the thinnest.
note: Labor carries ~47.7% margin vs ~31.5% on materials, 25.5% on equipment, and 23.6% on subcontracted work. Revenue mix toward labor (service, maintenance) drives higher blended margin than equipment- or sub-heavy work.

label: Bill rate by role (rate-card field)
definition: Median rate-card rate by field role across 18,000+ tracked employees. The rate-card field is used inconsistently (some enter customer billing rates, others loaded cost or base wage), so read the spread between roles rather than the absolute level. Company-level avg bill rate median is $79/hr (n=1,770).
basis: 18,000+ field employees with tracked rate-card data
note: The apprentice-to-journeyman jump (about $39 to $76) is the sharpest step in the ladder; journeymen carry the widest spread over loaded wage.
